pages.text: The seawater was calm as glass. Dad tossed a stone, and it skipped, skipped, skipped.
They wanted to make a stone skip three times too. "Let us try skip, skip, skip!"
Riri studied the stones at her feet. Lolo grabbed any stone. "Choose the stone first." "Just throw it hard."
Stones went into Riri's pocket one by one: flat stones, round stones, smooth stones.
Her pocket bulged. The weight made Riri waddle.
Lolo threw with all the strength possible. Plop—the stone sank at once.
Lolo threw even harder. Water splashed up, soaking Lolo.
A crab passed along the shore. Keeping its body low, it scuttled sideways.
"Low like the crab!" Riri pointed. When Lolo crouched low, Riri handed over a flat stone. It flew over the water.
Skip, skip, skip! The stone bounced three times, then slipped into the water. Still soaked, Lolo raised both arms high.
